title: Taking part with freedom to choose
meaning: Freely chosen participation can inspire you when careful attention separates the purpose of an endeavour from an obligatory reward.
text: Something important sometimes emerges through a question: would you want to participate without praise? The Devil in the energy of Sahasrara supports liberating awareness of attachment, noticing a promised reward and reclaiming your freedom to choose. The High Priestess in the physical position describes careful attention to the content beneath an attractive invitation. The Star in emotions brings hopeful generosity and a warm sense of involvement. You can enjoy the possibility that something useful will continue, even if neither of you sees the whole result or becomes the centre of attention.

For example, you consider an invitation to help with an open educational handbook. A promise to credit contributors on the cover catches your interest first, but reading the material makes the purpose itself more engaging. **Free participation leaves more room for meaning than a compulsory reward.** You choose a small section you can actually improve. Imagining strangers understanding a difficult subject feels rewarding; that hope connects your shared effort with someone else’s future understanding without promising you recognition.

The difficulty may appear if you endlessly investigate your hidden motives: is your interest pure enough, or does the cover still appeal? Attention moves from the material to examining every inward impulse. Conscious choice and generous hope remain supportive; participating does not require the complete absence of pleasant expectations. A useful correction can already be made and sent while those expectations remain.
